statement: Basal metabolic rate: Cunningham/Katch–McArdle from fat-free mass (370 + 21.6 × FFM kg) by default; Tinsley (24.8 × BW kg + 10) for very lean, advanced clients. Untrained clients with higher body fat get a flag to correct the estimate against weigh-ins.

quotes: the PTC recommends the Cunningham (1991) equation (BMR = 370 + 21.6 × FFM in kg, also known as Katch-McArdle)
if you're very lean and highly muscled, prefer Tinsley (24.8 × BW(kg) + 10)
Cunningham is a poor default for higher-body-fat, untrained people
bu.note: BU's formula choice. BU gives no cut-offs: 'very lean' uses the body-fat levels in params and 'highly muscled' means 4+ years of training; the 'unreliable' levels are set so BU's example (untrained woman, 30% body fat) is flagged. BU names no better formula for those clients, so they keep Katch–McArdle with a flag to correct it after 2+ weeks of weigh-ins (BU: treat any estimate as a starting point).

statement: Physical activity level for activity outside training, by sex. Resistance training is not in it: it is costed separately as training-day expenditure.

quotes: sedentary 1.00, light 1.11–1.12, active 1.25–1.27, very active 1.45–1.48, sex-specific
explicitly excluding resistance training from that multiplier
bu.note: BU values, excluding resistance training. BU gives each level as a range; which end is male and which female follows the IOM coefficients the ranges come from. 'values' (the midpoint) is used for 'anders' or an unknown sex.

statement: Thermic effect of food applied as a ×1.1 multiplier on BMR×PAL and on training energy expenditure.

quotes: the thermic effect of food (TEF) is layered on as a multiplier (BMR × TEF = REE), typically 10% as a population average
BMR × PAL × TEF ≈ non-training-day TDEE, or ((BMR × PAL) + RTEE) × TEF on training days
bu.note: Same multiplier and the same rest-day/training-day structure as ClientIntake.

statement: Training-day energy expenditure = MET × 3.5 × bodyweight / 200 × minutes.

quotes: 0.1 kcal/kg/min of active training time, roughly 300–500 kcal per session
bu.note: MET 5.7 over 60 minutes is about 0.1 kcal/kg/min, the BU figure.

statement: Energy-balance factor on maintenance. Fat loss: the deficit scales with body fat, from 2.5–7.5% near contest leanness to 30–50% at high body fat, linear in between. Muscle and strength goals: the surplus scales with training status (beginner 5–15%, intermediate 2–7%, advanced 1–3%). Maintenance: 1.0 ±3%.

quotes: scaled by training status (beginners 5–15% surplus targeting 0.5–1%/week bodyweight gain; intermediate 2–7% targeting 0.2–0.5%/week; advanced 1–3%
For cutting rate, the PTC scales the weekly rate of loss and the size of the deficit inversely with leanness
Start at ~20% deficit (Overgewicht category)
bu.note: BU's ranges at both ends. BU gives no body-fat cut-offs, so the anchors are a judgement call, chosen so BU's worked example (untrained woman, 30% body fat) lands on its ~20% deficit. The default at high body fat is the low end of 30–50%. Maintenance ±3% is not from BU.

statement: Protein 1.6–2.4 g/kg bodyweight per day; 1.8 g/kg practical default; not raised during a deficit.

quotes: never found a significant hypertrophy/strength benefit above 1.6 g/kg/day
the PTC still recommends 1.8 g/kg for advanced lifters
implies needs of 2.4+ g/kg
keep 1.6–2.2 g/kg as the working range
closer to linear than to a hard 1.6 g/kg breakpoint
Use fat-free mass to set targets for clients with high body fat.
bu.note: Matches: BU keeps 1.6–2.2 g/kg as the working range, the PTC default is 1.8 g/kg, 2.4+ g/kg for steroid users. BU's Nov 2026 update reads the dose-response as closer to linear than a hard 1.6 g/kg plateau and suggests fat-free mass as the basis for clients with high body fat; the plan still multiplies by bodyweight. Switching to fat-free mass is an open proposal and a calculation change, so it would go through ClientIntake first.

statement: Fat 20–40% of rest-day energy expenditure (REE): women 40% (top of the range), men 30% (middle), anders 35%.

quotes: the PTC recommends women target the higher end (closer to 40% of REE) of the 20-40% fat-intake range
treat 20-40% of calories from fat as a reasonable target
bu.note: BU puts women at the top of the 20–40% range. It sets no point for men, so they get the middle. The basis is REE, as in BU's PTC section (the 'What this means for you' list says calories).

statement: Meals per day used to split the macros.

quotes: the PTC's recommendation is 3-5 meals/day as a practical default
Meal number and size are about appetite and preference, not a cap.
bu.note: Default 4 within 3–5. The ad libitum module allows 2–5, and up to 6 in a bulk. BU's Nov 2026 update (Trommelen 2023) removes the per-meal protein cap, so fewer, larger meals are fine when a client prefers them.

statement: Post-training meals get 50% more protein; 100% more when only one meal sits between training and bed.

quotes: roughly 50-100% more per meal than pre-training meals
bu.note: ×1.5 (×2.0 with a single post-training meal) is 50–100% more.
